definitions.explanation: Having many tasks or engagements. Used as a polite way to describe being busy.

examples.english: Thank you for taking the time out of your busy schedule.

notes:
{多用|たよう} has two distinct uses: "frequent use" (sense 1) and "being busy" (sense 2).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {多用|たよう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to use frequently)
- {多用|たよう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{避|さ}ける→避ける：02109_sakeru⟧ (to avoid overuse)
- ご{多用|たよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ところ→ところ：01137_tokoro⟧ (despite your busy schedule — polite set phrase)

USAGE:
Sense 2 is primarily used in polite or formal expressions, especially in business correspondence. ご{多用|たよう} is a respectful way to acknowledge that someone is busy, similar to ご⟦{多忙|たぼう}→多忙：12166_tabou⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {多用|たよう} vs. ⟦{多様|たよう}→多様：12180_tayou⟧: Despite identical readings, these are different words. {多用|たよう} means "frequent use" or "busy," while ⟦{多様|たよう}→多様：12180_tayou⟧ means "diverse" or "varied."
